label.fr: Association et organisation à but non lucratif

expects.rule: The first screen states what the organisation does and who it helps, in plain words, before any appeal for money. NN/g found that users looked for trust information and rated finding it only 5.3 out of 7.
Show stories of people the work has helped. NN/g testers valued them more than mission statements on social media.
Keep the donation flow as short as a shop checkout. NN/g measured donating at 7% longer than an e-commerce checkout on average, with a 5.7 out of 7 rating for the process itself.
Give volunteers the typical duties and hours up front, and a way to talk to a person. NN/g notes people often want to speak to somebody before volunteering.
Do not push donations, products or newsletter sign-ups at every step. NN/g participants were annoyed by it.
A donate button is reachable from every page without scrolling back to the top, and the page says where the money goes.
Annual figures, legal status and contact details are one click from the first screen, so a donor can judge the organisation.

traits: 6 of 8 first screens are led by a photograph or film of people, a place or a building (Obama, Oregon, Higherlife, Zacamil, Re-Cycle, MobilityLab's map below); Climate TRACE uses a 3D globe and Illinois a graphic.
The headline is 12 words or fewer on 7 of 8, set at 46 to 198 px or larger than the body by at least 3x.
A donate, join or contact action is in the header on 6 of 8 (Obama, Oregon, Higherlife, Re-Cycle, Illinois, MobilityLab); only Obama, Re-Cycle and Illinois say donate.
4 of 8 use one typeface family (Higherlife, MobilityLab, Illinois, Climate TRACE); the other 4 pair a display or serif face with a sans or mono (Obama, Zacamil, Re-Cycle, Oregon).
One accent colour marks the action: lime on Higherlife and Re-Cycle, orange on Oregon, blue on Illinois; the rest is dark, grey or white.
6 of 8 have a header menu of 3 to 6 items; Climate TRACE and Colonia Zacamil have none on the first screen.
6 of 8 show a consent box or bar over part of the first screen.

sites.name: Obama Foundation
sites.why: Dark photograph of the Obama Presidential Center tower under a slate-blue banner for programme applications (deadline 2026-11-23); 'A campus that brings change home' in a grey condensed sans, a grey 'Donate' box in the header, five menu items. Serif body (Chronicle Text) and Gotham Condensed.
sites.recognition: Webby Award 2025, Charitable Organizations/Non-Profit, General Desktop & Mobile Sites (announced 2025-04-22)

sites.name: Climate TRACE
sites.why: 3D globe covered in orange bars on dark slate (#444546); headline 'Comprehensive Emissions Insight' and three stacked panels (Track Global Emissions, See Pollution Plumes, Estimate Emissions Reductions). Set in APK Protocol. No donate button.
sites.recognition: Webby Award 2025, Sustainability & Environment, General Desktop & Mobile Sites

sites.name: Oregon Outdoor Alliance
sites.why: Grey (#efeeee) page with a blurred black-and-white film of a cup in a machine; 'Connection. Cultivation. Business Growth.' in a grotesk (Manrope) with a monospaced label (IBM Plex Mono); orange 'Become a member' button, two news cards at right, cookie bar over the headline.

sites.name: Higherlife Foundation
sites.why: Full-bleed dimmed photograph of a person at a microscope; 46 px headline 'Building Africa's future. One person, one community, one purpose at a time.' in Cera Pro, a lime (#c6f886) 'Get Involved' button in the header and a lime 'What We Do' arrow. One typeface.

sites.name: Colonia Zacamil
sites.why: Beige (#ebe6e0) page: 'FLY TO ZACAMIL' in a tall condensed black display face with an aerial photograph of housing blocks inside a rounded slot between the words; a black 'Discover' pill; audio prompt below; consent panel at right. Reckless Neue, Heathergreen and Roboto Mono.

sites.name: MobilityLab
sites.why: White page with faint vertical grid lines: 64 px two-tone headline 'Expérimenter. Inspirer. Transformer la mobilité de demain, ici, au cœur des Alpes.' in Switzer, five partner logos, 'En savoir plus' button, FR/DE switch, black Contact button, 3D map of mountains below the fold.

sites.name: Re-Cycle
sites.why: Dark green photograph of a smiling boy on a bike with a man beside him; 81 px headline 'DONATE A BIKE. CHANGE A LIFE.' in Rubik, white and lime (#c8df0a); two Donate buttons in the header and a 'Donate A Bike' button; phone and email in a lime top strip. DM Sans for text.
sites.recognition: Awwwards Nominee, 2026-11-11 (voting open, no award yet)

sites.name: Illinois Innocence Project
sites.why: Saturated blue (#405bf7) panel with 'Advocate. Educate. Reform.' at 86 px in TASA Orbiter and a huge striped '25 You're invited' graphic in navy, lime and lilac; one sentence of text; Request Help and Donate in a top strip. No photograph.

avoid: Stock photos of smiling children or hands holding a globe in place of real people and places.
A donation form that asks for an account or many fields before the amount.
Impact claims without a figure, a date or a named programme.
A pop-up asking for a gift or newsletter sign-up on arrival.
Social media feeds embedded as main content: NN/g found people do not use Facebook to research non-profits.
Non-monetary giving (items, volunteering) hidden in the footer: NN/g rated finding item donations 5.3 out of 7, the lowest score in its study.

sources.name: Nielsen Norman Group, Non-Profit Websites: Donations
